newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Left under pressure to block Le Pen in town.
newsitem.headline: French Left under pressure to block Le Pen in town.

text.p: France's opposition Socialists were under pressure to rally behind the ruling conservatives on Monday to stop the extreme-right National Front of Jean-Marie Le Pen capturing control of a fourth town in a local election.

National Front candidate Marie-France Stirbois topped the poll in Dreux, a town of 36,000 west of Paris, in Sunday's first round with 36.5 percent of the vote, closely followed by outgoing Gaullist mayor Gerard Hamel with 34.7 percent.
The outcome of next Sunday's runoff may depend on the attitude of the united Left list led by Socialist Maurice Ravanne, who won just under 25 percent, enough to stay in the race if he so chooses.

Julien Dray, a member of the Socialist party's national leadership, called on the Left to drop out and throw its support behind the mainstream conservatives to prevent the anti-immigration Front winning control.
"We have to stand down. There's nothing else we can do," Dray told France-Inter radio. "In the second round, it's clear we must prevent the National Front getting its hands on Dreux."
Conservative politicians ruled out any formal alliance with the Left that might have given left-wing candidates places on a joint slate, saying voters did not want that.
"There is no point in calling for a "republican front' because that's not what the majority wants," veteran Gaullist Jacques Baumel said.
So the Socialists have the choice between simply dropping out or staying in the race at the risk of handing the mayor's seat to the National Front.

Despite a personal visit by Le Pen to Dreux, where the Front scored its first breakthrough in politics in 1983, Stirbois barely improved her score from last year's municipal election, invalidated by a court due to irregularities involving Hamel.

In the campaign, Stirbois fulminated against immigrants who she says intimidate "native French people' and take their jobs, and pledged to give the local police paramilitary training and dog squads to stamp out delinquency.
Unemployment is well above the national average of 12.6 percent in a town heavily populated by North African immigrants.
Hamel said Sunday's first round result, in which he gained nearly seven points over last year, showed voters did not want the National Front.
"The National Front will never win Dreux," he declared.
